original_question: How should the nuclear energy density functional be extended so that it can make reliable predictions at the drip lines? This includes explaining the Wigner energy in nuclei with equal neutron and proton numbers near the proton drip line, determining whether isoscalar T = 0 pairing is responsible for that extra binding, and constructing a functional that remains valid despite incomplete knowledge of low-density clustering and high-density many-body interactions, so that empirical data near the drip lines can properly constrain the functional form.
target_in_paper: In Section 3.1, the paper states: “A major problem at the proton drip line is related to the Wigner energy in nuclei. It cannot be explained by conventional density functionals and its extension is necessary. There are some arguments that the isoscalar (T=0) pairing might be responsible for the Wigner energy, but it is not conclusive yet. The exact solution is unknown even at these low- and high-density limits because of nuclear clustering at low density and the lack of knowledge about three-body interactions at high density. Thus, empirical information near the drip lines provides indispensable information about the nuclear density functional.”
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the need to extend the nuclear energy density functional to account for the Wigner energy at the proton drip line, the investigation of possible isoscalar T=0 pairing contributions, and the incorporation of low-density clustering and high-density many-body interactions with empirical constraints from drip-line nuclei.
missing_details: Definition of the universal energy density functional E[ρ] and the pairing (abnormal) density functional E_pair[\tildeρ].
Explicit statement that the Wigner energy refers to extra binding in N=Z nuclei near the proton drip line.
Clarification that nuclear DFT lacks known analytic limits at low and high densities, unlike electronic DFT.
Mention that low-density clustering and unknown high-density three-body forces preclude exact solutions.
Specification that empirical drip-line data complement the lack of stable-nuclei data at saturation density ρ₀ to constrain the functional form.
Scope restriction to the open problems formulated in Section 3.1 regarding extensions of the energy density functional including the continuum.
refined_question: How can the universal nuclear energy density functional E[ρ] and its associated pairing functional E_pair[\tildeρ] be systematically extended so as to (i) reproduce the extra binding (Wigner energy) observed in N=Z nuclei near the proton drip line—potentially through an isoscalar (T=0) pairing term—and (ii) span regimes of low-density clustering and high-density three-body interactions, for which no exact analytic limits are known, thereby enabling empirical data on drip-line nuclei (at densities ρ<<ρ₀ and ρ>>ρ₀) to constrain the functional form?
justification: This refinement directly mirrors the open problem posed in Section 3.1 of the paper, which highlights the inability of existing functionals to explain the Wigner energy at the proton drip line, the inconclusive role of isoscalar pairing, and the lack of theoretical guidance at low and high density due to clustering and three-body forces, hence the necessity of empirical drip-line data to determine both E[ρ] and E_pair[\tildeρ].
